title: Canonical completed integral scalar data and constant sections
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E,L$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and let $\iota:E\to L$ be a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra embedding, with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E,\mathcal O_L$, chosen uniformizers and quotient rings $A_{H,n+1}=\mathcal O_H/\varpi_H^{n+1}$ for $H=E,L$ and $n\geq0$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $Y$ be a scheme with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and completed coefficient ring sheaves $R_H=\varprojlim_{n\geq0}(A_{H,n+1})_Y$ with projections $\pi_{H,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Define the following canonical scalar data. The ring homomorphism $j:\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_L$ is the restriction of $\iota$ to the valuation rings. It induces $j_n:A_{E,n+1}\to A_{L,n+1}$. Define $c:R_E\to R_L$ to be the unique morphism whose composite with $\pi_{L,n}$ is $(j_n)_Y\circ\pi_{E,n}$ for every $n$. For any sheaf $M$ of $R_E$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], define ordinary scalar extension $T(M)=R_L\otimes_{R_E}M$ by sheafifying the presheaf tensor, with its canonical functor on morphisms [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], using the ordinary change-of-rings witness of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For every site object $U$, $s\in R_L(U)$ and $x\in M(U)$, define $\tau_{M,U}(s,x)\in T(M)(U)$ as the image of the pure tensor $s\otimes x$ under the sheafification unit and the canonical identification with this ordinary extension. Define $d=[L:E]$ using the $E$-algebra structure on $L$ induced by $\iota$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. For $a\in\mathcal O_H$, define $a_{n,U}\in(A_{H,n+1})_Y(U)$ to be the constant section obtained by applying the sheafification unit to the residue of $a$, and define $a_U\in R_H(U)$ as the unique section satisfying $\pi_{H,n}(a_U)=a_{n,U}$ for every $n$. The scheme and coefficient universes are independent. These are constructions, with no finite-freeness or sections-tensor isomorphism assertion.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), pp. 58-59 (completed coefficient sheaves and coefficient extension); Proposition 6.8.14(1), p. 61 (scalar extension); ordinary sheafified tensor as in Stacks Tag 03EK. The constant sections and coefficient inclusion are the inverse-limit constructions used in the explicit point sections calculation.
